NARRATIVE AND PLANS FOR TYPE 1 ZONING AMENDMENT FOR
2156 WEST WARREN BOULEVARD, CHICAGO

The subject property is a Transit Served Location, as it is situated within 250° of Madison Bus
Corridor and within 1,500’ of CTA Green Line Station at Damen. It is currently a vacant
unimproved zoning lot. The Applicant intends to redevelop this property with a new 4-story
residential building with 8 dwelling units and 5 outdoor parking spaces located at the rear of the
property. The Applicant needs a zoning change to an RMS, Residential Multi-Unit District with
optional variation relief for rear yard open space and front and side setbacks to comply with the
standards and the bulk requirements of the Ordinance for this redevelopment project.

Project Zoning Change from the RT4, Residential Two-Flat, Townhouse and
Description: Multi-Unit District to an RM5 Residential Multi-Unit District

Use: Residential Building with 8 Dwelling Units and 5 parking spaces.

I. Optional Relief for Adjustment and Variation under Section 17-13-0303-D —

a Type 1 map amendment pursuant to Section 17-13-0300, may include relief available
pursuant to Section 17-13-1000 or 17-13-1100; in such instances, City Council approval of a
Type-1 application containing said elements shall preclude subsequent review otherwise
required pursuant to Sections 17-13-1000 or 17-13-1100, provided that no Type 1
application permits issued may be in violation of Section 17-13-0310:

(A) The Applicant also seeks relief for variations under section 17-13-1101-B as follows:

(1) From side setback requirements of Section 17-2-0309-A, which states that when a side
lot line abuts an alley or street, no side setback is required on the side of the building
abutting the street or alley, but in such cases, the side setback on the other (non-street
or alley) side must be at least 10% of the lot's width. Since the west side of the
building abuts Leavitt St., it requires east side setback of 4.75”. As the building is
designed with a 2’ west side setback, the Applicant requests a reduction in the east
side setback from 4.75’ required to 3’-6” proposed, and the combined side setbacks
from 9.5’ required to 5.5° proposed

(2) From the front setback requirements of Section 17-2-0305-B, which states that
buildings in RM districts must be set back from the front property line a distance
equal to either: the minimum front setback standard of 15 feet or the average front
yard depth that exists on the nearest 2 lots on either side of the subject lot. Since

majority of the neighboring lots are vacant, the Applicant is requesting a variation to
reduce the front setback from 15’ required to 8” proposed.

(B) The Applicant also seeks relief for variation under Section 17-13-1101-A and 17-13-
1003-K, from the rear yard open space requirements of Section 17-2-0307 Rear Yard
Open Space. Section 17-2-0307 states that developments in RMS districts are subject to
minimum rear yard open space of 36 square feet per dwelling unit or 5.25% of lot area,
whichever is greater, with 10’ diameter of a circle that must fit within that rear yard open
space. While the design provides about 376 SF of open space in the rear plus private
balconies, such open space doesn’t strictly comply with the technical requirements;

therefore, the Applicant is requesting a reduction in the rear yard open space from 332 SF
required to zero proposed.

(C) The Applicant is seeking all relief necessary, as allowed by the Zoning Ordinance, for the
proposed development per the attached Type 1 Plans.

In support of this request, the Applicant states the following:

1. Strict compliance with the applicable Zoning Ordinance requirements would create
practical difficulties and unnecessary hardship for the subject property due to its unique
physical configuration, corner lot location, and surrounding conditions, where majority of
the subject block remains vacant and undeveloped. The requested variations are intended
to allow the property to be developed in a reasonable and compatible manner while
preserving substantial open space, setbacks, and separation from neighboring properties to
the extent reasonably practicable.

Py The requested variations are consistent with the stated purpose and intent of this Zoning
Ordinance since this proposed redevelopment and corresponding variations are compatible
with the existing land use pattern on the subject block. Furthermore, the new dwelling

units will increase the variety of available housing stock, as the Ordinance intends, in
Tesponse to the growing housing demand in the neighborhood.

3. Evidence of Practica] Difficulties or Particular Hardship is as follows:

- The property in question cannot yield a reasonable return if permitted to be used only
in accordance with the strict standards of this Zoning Ordinance. This proposed
redevelopment is intended to provide additional dwelling units in a high-density
community which has been designated as a Downtown Area. Potential new residents
are looking for modern efficient floor plans, with more functional open space and on-
site parking. The proposed variations will allow the Applicant to meet these market
demands.

- Strict compliance with Section 17-2-0309-A, would require a 4'-9" setback along the
east side and zero along west side, while the proposed building already provides a 3'-
6" east setback and a 2'-0" west setback. Requiring the additional 1'-3" of east setback
would unnecessarily reduce the buildable area of an already constrained site and
would make it substantially more difficult to achieve a functional building
configuration. The proposed setbacks continue to provide meaningful separation from
the adjacent properties and public way, while allowing the building to maintain a
practical and functional footprint.

- Strict compliance with the 15-foot front setback requirement would also create a
practical difficulty because the surrounding development pattern does not provide a
consistent established front yard from which a meaningful contextual setback can be
derived. A majority of the neighboring lots are vacant, making it difficult to establish a
fepresentative average front yard depth based upon surrounding development.
Requiring the full 15-foot setback under these circumstances would impose a setback
that is not reflective of a consistent established neighborhood condition. The proposed
8-foot front setback allows the building to be appropriately positioned on the property
while maintaining a meaningful setback from the public way.

- The request for the rear yard open space reduction represents technical
dimensional/configuration noncompliance, rather than an actual elimination of open
space. Although the plans provide approximately 376 square feet of rear yard open
space, with additional private open space provided by the proposed balconies, the
configuration does not satisfy all of the technical requirements of Section 17-2-0307,
including the required dimensional configuration and 10-foot-diameter circle
requirement. Requiring the rear yard to be reconfigured solely to satisfy the technical
requirements would unnecessarily constrain the property's development without
providing a corresponding meaningful benefit, particularly where substantial outdoor
space is already being provided.

- The practical difficulties and particular hardships are due to unique circumstances and
are not generally applicable to other similarly situated properties. The property has a
unique location, as it has frontage on two public rights-of-way, ensuring that there will
be adequate light and air provided to the proposed building and no adverse effect to
the light and air of adjacent properties.

- These variations will not alter the essential character of the neighborhood, since there
are other zoning lots within this neighborhood which also do not strictly comply with
the current underlying bulk requirements. This proposed redevelopment has been
designed to follow the existing land use pattern in the area, as the Ordinance mandates.
